problems.title: A sum minus one addend
problems.question: Two numbers have a sum 8 greater than one of them and 25 greater than the other. Find the numbers.
problems.idea: Subtracting an addend leaves the other addend.
formulas: If x+y=x+8 and x+y=y+25, then y=8,x=25.

problems.title: Cubic unit conversion
problems.question: A rectangular reservoir measures 1.2 km by 0.8 km by 2.5 km. How many litres does it hold?
problems.idea: Convert kilometres to decimetres before interpreting litres.

problems.title: Divisibility by 36
problems.question: 123AB is divisible by 36. How many distinct values can A+B have?
problems.idea: Use divisibility by both 9 and 4.
formulas: Digit sum=6+A+B; last two digits 10A+B must be divisible by 4.
steps: Since 0≤A+B≤18, divisibility by 9 gives A+B=3 or 12.
Both occur: AB=12 gives 12312 divisible by 36, and AB=48 gives 12348 divisible by 36.
There are exactly two possible sums.

problems.title: Bisectors of the outer parts of a straight angle
problems.question: A straight angle is divided into consecutive parts in ratio 4:6:8. Find the angle between the first and third parts’ bisectors.
problems.idea: Find the unit angle from the ratio sum.
steps: The bisectors are 20° and 40° inside the outer angles.

problems.title: The last day is a quarter of the trip
problems.question: Tourists travel 3/8 of a route on day 1 and 3/5 of the remainder on day 2. Day 3 takes 3 h 20 min at the same speed. Find total travel time.
problems.idea: Time fractions equal distance fractions at constant speed.
steps: The last day is one quarter of the full trip.
Its time is 200 minutes, so total moving time is 800 minutes.

problems.title: Last digits of powers
problems.question: Find the last digit of 199²⁰¹⁶-2016¹⁹⁹.
problems.idea: Work modulo 10.
steps: The difference is congruent to 1-6=-5≡5 modulo 10.

problems.title: Triangles from two parallel lines
problems.question: Four points lie on one line and five on a parallel line. Count triangles with these vertices.
problems.idea: A nondegenerate triangle uses two points from one line and one from the other.
steps: The two cases give 30 and 40 triangles.

problems.title: Reverse a fraction relationship
problems.question: a is 2/3 of b. What percent of a is b?
problems.idea: Solve for b/a.

problems.title: Filter a finite set
problems.question: A is the two-digit multiples of 9, B the integers with remainder 3 modulo 4, C the numbers below 100 ending in 3. Count (A∩B)\C.
problems.idea: List the small intersection first.
steps: Of those, 63 ends in 3 and is removed.

problems.title: Supplementary angles with proportional parts
problems.question: Two supplementary angles satisfy (2/7) of one =0.4 of the other. Find their difference.
problems.idea: Combine the ratio with the sum 180°.

problems.title: A diagonal splits the polygon’s boundary
problems.question: Vertices 42 and 81 of a convex 100-gon are joined. How many sides do the two resulting polygons have?
problems.idea: Count each boundary path, then add the new diagonal.
formulas: One path has 81-42=39 edges; the other has 100-39=61.
steps: The diagonal adds one side to each polygon.
Thus the counts are 40 and 62; together they total 102 because the diagonal is counted twice.

problems.title: Same cost for fewer litres
problems.question: Last year 10 litres of fuel cost as much as 8 litres now. Find the percentage price increase.
problems.idea: Let the old per-litre price be p.
steps: The increase relative to the old price is (5/4-1)·100%=25%.

problems.title: The source says a line, not a circle
problems.question: A,B,C,D lie in that order on a line. AC=8,BD=12,AD=17. Find the distance between the midpoints of BC and AD.
problems.idea: Choose A as coordinate 0.
problems.note: The scanned Georgian says the points lie on a straight line. A transcription incorrectly says a circle; the linear reading is used here.

problems.title: Vertical angles and a ray division
problems.question: Lines MN and RP cross at O. ∠MOP+∠RON=60°. OS divides ∠PON in ratio POS:SON=3:2. Find ∠MOS.
problems.idea: The two given angles are vertical and equal.

problems.title: Parallel inconsistent equations
problems.question: For which a does y-ax=4, ax+2y=6x-2 have no solution?
problems.idea: Substitute the first equation into the second.
steps: If 3a-6≠0, there is exactly one x and one y.
If a=2, the equation becomes 0=-10, impossible.

problems.title: Combine repeated prime factors
problems.question: Count positive divisors of 2²·5²·7³·4.
problems.idea: Absorb 4 into the power of 2.
steps: Choose the exponent of 2 in 5 ways, of 5 in 3 ways, and of 7 in 4 ways.

problems.title: An angle is determined by two rays
problems.question: Ten distinct rays are drawn inside a right angle. How many angles have two of those rays as sides?
problems.idea: Choose an unordered pair of the ten new rays.
steps: Every pair determines one angle less than 90°.
problems.note: This counts the ten new rays only, as indicated by the listed answer. Including the original two boundary rays would give C(12,2)=66.

problems.title: Recover two omitted angles
problems.question: A transversal crosses parallel lines. Six of the eight angles sum to 500°. Find the smallest angle.
problems.idea: All eight angles sum to 720°.
formulas: The two omitted angles sum to 720°-500°=220°.
steps: The omitted pair cannot consist of one acute and one obtuse angle, since those sum to 180°.
It must be two equal 110° angles.

problems.title: A linear combination of residues
problems.question: a≡2 and b≡3 modulo 7. Find the remainder of 4a-3b.
problems.idea: Replace each input by its residue.

problems.title: Compare fractions with decimal bounds
problems.question: Which listed fraction lies strictly between 0.7 and 0.8?
problems.idea: Compare 7/9 to both endpoints.
steps: Thus 7/9≈0.7778 is in the desired interval.
The other listed fractions are either below 0.7 or above 0.8.

problems.title: Divisors of a product of prime powers
problems.question: Count positive divisors of 81·125.
problems.idea: Factor the two numbers.
steps: The exponents of 3 and 5 can be selected independently.

problems.title: GCD times LCM equals the product
problems.question: Two natural numbers have gcd·lcm=111 and differ by 34. Find their sum.
problems.idea: Use the factor pairs of 111.
steps: The positive factor pairs are (1,111) and (3,37).

problems.title: A negative linear slope
problems.question: Which listed function decreases on all of ℝ?
problems.idea: A linear function with negative slope decreases strictly everywhere.
formulas: For y=mx+b, m<0 implies strict decrease.
steps: The constant and piecewise functions fail strict decrease, or reverse direction somewhere.
problems.note: Under a non-strict “nonincreasing” convention, y=10 also qualifies; the listed intended meaning is strictly decreasing.

problems.title: Minimum after horizontal and vertical changes
problems.question: f is defined on ℝ with minimum 2. Find the minimum of 2f(3x-5)+4.
problems.idea: The inner linear expression still ranges over all real inputs.
steps: Multiply the minimum by 2 and add 4: 2·2+4=8.

problems.title: Midline from perpendicular diagonals
problems.question: A trapezoid has perpendicular diagonals of lengths 3 and 4. Find its midline.
problems.idea: Use the vector difference of diagonals to recover the base sum.
steps: The midline is half the base sum.

problems.title: A weighted concentration
problems.question: Mix 3 litres of 30% alcohol solution with 5 litres of 20% solution. Find the resulting percentage.
problems.idea: Add the alcohol amounts and divide by total volume.
steps: The total is 8 litres, assuming the volume-addition convention of the problem.

problems.title: Reduce into one period
problems.question: f has period 1 and f(x)=|x| on [-1/2,1/2]. Find f(π+2).
problems.idea: Subtract an integer to reach the stated interval.
steps: Since π-3>0, its absolute value is π-3.

problems.title: The quadrant selects a sign
problems.question: B=(a-1,4+a²) lies in quadrant II and is 29 from the x-axis. Find a.
problems.idea: The vertical coordinate is positive.
steps: Only a=-5 makes the x-coordinate negative.

problems.title: Difference of fourth powers of conjugates
problems.question: Evaluate [(2+√3)⁴-(2-√3)⁴]/(56√3).
problems.idea: Square each conjugate first.

problems.title: Two roots of the same power
problems.question: Evaluate ⁵√(a²√a)·∛(a²√a) at a=8.
problems.idea: Use rational exponents.

problems.title: An isosceles trapezoid’s diagonal
problems.question: A trapezoid has larger base 2 cm and its other three sides all 1 cm. Find a diagonal.
problems.idea: Centre the shorter base over the longer one.

problems.title: Clear a linear inequality carefully
problems.question: Solve 3x-(2x+1)/2>4-(2-x)/3-x.
problems.idea: Simplify each side or multiply by 6.

problems.title: A radical expression simplifies after substitution
problems.question: Simplify [(a+2)/√(2a)-a/(√(2a)+2)+2/(a-√(2a))]·(√a-√2)/(a+2).
problems.idea: Let v=√(a/2), so a=2v² and √(2a)=2v.

problems.title: Split a combined work rate
problems.question: Two teams together finish a job in 12 hours. Their rates are in ratio 3:2. How long would team 1 take alone?
problems.idea: Team 1 supplies 3/5 of the total rate.
steps: Time for one whole job is the reciprocal of the rate.

problems.title: Distances from a circumcenter to right-triangle legs
problems.question: A right triangle is inscribed in a radius-√3 circle. One leg is √3 times closer to the centre than the other. Find the larger leg.
problems.idea: The circumcenter is the hypotenuse midpoint.
formulas: Distances from that midpoint to the legs equal half the other leg; hypotenuse=2√3.
steps: The legs therefore have ratio √3:1. Write them √3t,t.

problems.title: A chord at a known centre distance
problems.question: In an isosceles triangle, the circumcenter is 7 from vertex B and 1 from base AC. Find AC.
problems.idea: The first distance is the radius.

problems.title: Distance from the origin to a line
problems.question: Find the distance from (0,0) to 3x-4y=12.
problems.idea: Use the point-to-line distance formula.

problems.title: A trapezoid with both an incircle and circumcircle
problems.question: A trapezoid has an incircle and a circumcircle. Its base sum equals the circumcircle diameter, and its diagonal is 20. Find the inradius.
problems.idea: A cyclic trapezoid is isosceles; tangency fixes its leg length.
formulas: Let bases B,b, leg l,height h,circumradius R. Then B+b=2l and R=ld/(2h).
steps: The given diameter condition B+b=2R gives l=R.
Substitute in R=ld/(2h) to obtain d=2h.
Since d=20, h=10. The incircle touches both parallel bases, so 2r=h.

problems.title: A moving row reverses at a moving coach
problems.question: Athletes form a row of length m and run at 20 km/h toward a coach running at 15 km/h. Each athlete turns on meeting the coach, keeping speed 20. Find the row length after all turn.
problems.idea: Compare the first and last athletes’ meeting times.
steps: Take the first meeting at position 0,time 0. The coach moves to -15m/35 before meeting the last athlete.
The first athlete has meanwhile moved to -20m/35.
Their separation is (20-15)m/35=m/7. All athletes now move in the same direction, preserving that length.

problems.title: Lattice points on a segment
problems.question: A=(3,4),B=(6,8),D=(17,4) are vertices of parallelogram ABCD. Count integer-coordinate points on diagonal AC.
problems.idea: Find the fourth vertex and use the gcd of coordinate differences.
steps: Thus only the two endpoints are lattice points.
problems.answer: 2 including endpoints; 0 strictly inside the diagonal.
